questions.question: When a green arrow changes to a solid green light, what should you do?

options.text: You can still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
You must go straight and cannot turn.
You still have the right-of-way to turn.
You no longer need to turn in the direction the arrow pointed.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow changes to a solid green light, you can still turn in the direction the arrow pointed. However, you must first yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A sharp turn is ahead. Slow down.
There is a work crew ahead.
A side road is ahead.
A playground is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A sharp turn is ahead. Slow down.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions and dangers. This sign warns you that a sharp turn is coming and you should reduce your speed.

questions.question: You come to an intersection with a flashing red light. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.
Turn right or left because the road is blocked ahead.
Stop and wait for a flashing green light.
Stop, then go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop. After stopping, you can go when the road is clear and it is safe to proceed.

questions.question: On a road with three or more lanes, you must stop for a school bus with flashing red lights when:

options.text: You are traveling in any direction.
You are traveling toward the bus.
Children are crossing the road.
You are traveling in the same direction as the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are traveling in the same direction as the bus.
questions.explanation: You must stop for a flashing school bus in most situations. However, on a road with three or more lanes or with a median, you do not have to stop if the bus is going the opposite direction. You must stop if you are going the same direction as the bus.

questions.question: What is the most important thing to remember about speed and curves?

options.text: Drive at the speed limit as you enter, then slow down at the sharpest part.
Slow down before you enter the curve.
Speed up gently before you enter the curve.
Drive at the speed limit before, during, and after the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle may be hard to control in a curve because of its weight and motion. To stay in control, you must slow down before entering the curve.

questions.question: If your car starts to skid, which way should you turn your steering wheel?

options.text: Keep the front wheels straight.
In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
Opposite to the direction of the skid.
It does not matter which direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
questions.explanation: When your car skids, turn the steering wheel in the direction you want the vehicle to go. Once the vehicle straightens out, turn the wheel back the other way.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Only use your mirrors.
Start signaling as you move into the next lane.
Signal 500 feet before changing lanes on residential streets.
Always check your blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always check your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Other vehicles can hide in your blind spot. Always look over your shoulder before changing lanes. Signal 100 feet before a lane change on residential streets and 5 seconds before on freeways.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads, what should you do?

options.text: Always drive at the maximum speed limit.
Use cruise control to keep a steady speed.
Follow other cars more closely.
Avoid sudden changes in speed or direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden changes in speed or direction.
questions.explanation: Do not make sudden changes to your speed or direction on slippery roads. Reduce your speed and do not use cruise control on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: By law, when must your vehicle's headlights be on?

options.text: From one hour after sunset until one hour before sunrise.
From one hour before sunset until one hour after sunrise.
From 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise.
From 30 minutes before sunset until 30 minutes after sunrise.

questions.correctAnswerText: From 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise.
questions.explanation: By law, your headlights must be on from half an hour after sunset until half an hour before sunrise.

questions.question: What is a safe way to drive through a curve?

options.text: Slow down as you enter, speed up as you exit.
Keep the same speed throughout the curve.
Speed up as you enter, slow down as you exit.
Stay near the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you enter, speed up as you exit.
questions.explanation: Slow down as you enter a curve and speed up gradually as you exit. Speeding up when entering a curve makes it harder to control your vehicle.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spots when changing lanes?

options.text: Use the inside rearview mirror.
Use the outside rearview mirror.
Use both the inside and outside rearview mirrors.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Always turn your head to check your blind spots before you change lanes.

questions.question: How do smoked marijuana and marijuana-infused foods compare in terms of risk?

options.text: They have the same risks.
They have different risks.
They have few side effects when mixed with alcohol.
They will not affect your driving ability.

questions.correctAnswerText: They have different risks.
questions.explanation: Marijuana-infused food affects your body more slowly than smoked marijuana. Smoking marijuana can hurt your lungs. Both forms can damage your ability to drive safely.

questions.question: How should you treat railroad crossings?

options.text: They are safe to cross because trains are unlikely to come.
They are dangerous.
They are safe places to park your car.
They are places where you must always stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are dangerous.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are always dangerous. Look and listen for trains from both directions. Follow all signs, signals, and instructions from flaggers. Never cross until you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: What should you do first when you cannot see the road clearly?

options.text: Turn on your headlights.
Reduce your speed.
Turn on your windshield wipers.
Look for road edge markings to guide you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed.
questions.explanation: Slow down first when visibility is poor or road conditions are dangerous.

questions.question: When should you leave more space than usual between your car and the car in front of you?

options.text: When you are on a hill.
When you are at an intersection.
When you are at a stop sign.
When you are at a toll plaza.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are on a hill.
questions.explanation: Leave extra space when stopped on an uphill slope. If the car in front rolls backward when traffic moves, you have more time to react and avoid a crash.

questions.question: Your gas pedal gets stuck on a busy street. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn.
Press hard on the brakes.
Turn on your four-way flashers.
Turn off the engine carefully without locking the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the engine carefully without locking the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: If your gas pedal sticks, the car will keep going fast. Turn off the engine gently—only turn the key enough to stop the engine, not so much that it locks the steering wheel. Then use your brakes and move to a safe area.

questions.question: What should drivers do when driving in bad weather?

options.text: Drive faster to get where they are going more quickly.
Stay closer to the car in front.
Stay farther behind the car in front.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind the car in front.
questions.explanation: On wet roads, increase the distance between you and the car ahead of you.

questions.question: You see a flashing yellow light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait for the light to change.
Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.
Drive carefully through the intersection.
Get ready to stop; the light is about to turn red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive carefully through the intersection.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means proceed slowly and carefully. Look both ways before crossing.

questions.question: When you get in a car to drive, what should you adjust first?

options.text: Your seat belt.
The steering wheel.
Your rearview mirror.
Your seat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your seat.
questions.explanation: First adjust your seat so you are comfortable and can see the road. Then adjust your mirrors and steering wheel based on your seat position.

questions.question: A school bus is parked on the side of the road with no flashing lights. What should you do?

options.text: Stop no matter which side of the road you are on.
Stop until the bus driver tells you to go.
Stop only if you are on the same side of the road as the bus.
Pass carefully because you do not have to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pass carefully because you do not have to stop.
questions.explanation: You must stop for a school bus with red flashing lights on any side of the road. If the bus has no flashing lights or stop arm, you may pass with caution.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No passing zone
Wrong way
Railroad crossing
Stop

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zone
questions.explanation: Pennant-shaped signs show a no passing zone.

questions.question: You must pull over and let an emergency vehicle pass:

options.text: No matter which direction it is coming from.
Only if it is behind you.
Only if it is coming toward you.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: No matter which direction it is coming from.
questions.explanation: Pull to the right and stop for any emergency vehicle with flashing lights, whether it is behind you or coming from the other direction.

questions.question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed from the side with the broken line.
Passing is allowed from the side with the solid line.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from the side with the broken line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means you can pass only from the lane with the broken line.

questions.question: If you need to stop quickly and your vehicle does not have an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), you should:

options.text: Press and hold the brake pedal down.
Pump the brakes firmly.
Tap the brakes lightly.
Release the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pump the brakes firmly.
questions.explanation: Pumping the brakes helps you stop quickly while keeping control of your steering.

questions.question: Regulatory signs:

options.text: Are placed everywhere there is danger.
Tell drivers what they must or must not do.
Are diamond-shaped and yellow or green.
Warn drivers of school zones.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell drivers what they must or must not do.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are usually rectangular and white with black markings. They tell drivers what to do or not do, such as speed limits or no passing rules.
